exposure: Institutional policy changes related to the COVID-19 pandemic
Patient behaviors related to the COVID-19 pandemic
outcome: Perinatal composite outcome (delivery ≥ 41 weeks, hypertensive disorder of pregnancy at term, unplanned Cesarean delivery, term neonatal intensive care unit admission, 42-day maternal readmission, and 7-day neonatal readmission)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies delivered at a single institution with low incidence of COVID-19
finding: Significant changes in clinical practice occurred during the COVID-19 pandemic, including fewer inductions, more women presenting in labor, and more women delivering at or after 41 weeks, but these changes did not significantly affect overall perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Women in the COVID-19 group (March 15, 2020, through June 15, 2020) were more likely to present in spontaneous labor and less likely to undergo induction compared to the pre-COVID-19 group (December 15, 2019 through March 14, 2020).
